_meta.indication: Ga 68 DOTATOC Injection is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with PET for localization of somatostatin receptor positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult and pediatric patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-center, open-label study; Ga-68 DOTATOC PET images were rated by two independent readers blinded to clinical information as positive or negative for NET, compared to a composite reference of histopathology and imaging.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with known or suspected somatostatin receptor (SSTR) positive tumors referred for diagnosis or evaluation of disease extension; 178 of 220 (81%) had a history of neoplasm.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Positive percent agreement and negative percent agreement (reader agreement with composite reference) for detection of NET.
pivotal_trials.n: 220 enrolled; 177 in the efficacy analysis population
pivotal_trials.result: N=177: positive percent agreement 91% (95% CI 85, 95) and negative percent agreement 89% (95% CI 75, 96) for reader 1; 90% (84, 95) and 86% (73, 95) for reader 2.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-center, open-label study comparing Ga-68 DOTATOC PET/CT against a composite gold-standard reference including conventional imaging and clinical follow-up; images independently re-reviewed by two nuclear medicine physicians blinded to clinical data.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with histologically positive NET or other SSTR positive tumor referred for evaluation of disease before or after treatment.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Positive and negative percent agreement (reader agreement with composite reference) for detection of NET.
pivotal_trials.n: 62 enrolled; 59 in the efficacy analysis population
pivotal_trials.result: Positive and negative percent agreements were 92% and 75% for reader 1 and 90% and 75% for reader 2.

key_safety: Of 334 patients, 50 (15%) reported 75 AEs; 96% were CTCAE Grade 1 and no deaths or serious adverse events occurred. Most frequent AEs were nausea (2.1%), flushing (0.9%), and headache (0.9%). Labeled adverse reactions: nausea, pruritus, and flushing.
target_moa: Ga-68-DOTATOC binds to somatostatin receptors, with highest affinity for subtype 2 (SSTR2), which are overexpressed on certain malignant cells including neuroendocrine tumors, allowing their localization by PET.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA review.

orphan_indication.text: The drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, exempting the application from the PREA pediatric assessment requirement.

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: NDA 210828 was a standard-review 505(b)(2) application for a new molecular entity, approved first cycle based on a retrospective analysis of three prospective clinical trials (RET-NET-01) and a literature meta-analysis; of these, the review team identified Studies 1 and 2 (Study A and Study B) as sufficiently reliable for inclusion in labeling to support efficacy. The product carries an orphan drug designation for this indication.
